newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: POLL-MALAYSIA 1997 GDP GROWTH SEEN AT 7.9 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLL-MALAYSIA 1997 GDP GROWTH SEEN AT 7.9 PCT.

text.p: Malaysia's economic growth is expected to slow down further this year and in 1998 due to slower exports and lower investment inflows, economists said on Tuesday.
In a poll by Reuters, 12 research houses forecast an average of 7.9 percent for gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1997 against the government's forecast of 7.8-8.2 percent.
They forecast 1998 GDP growth at an average 7.4 percent.
Malaysia reported GDP growth of 8.2 percent in 1996.
Economists said they had mostly revised down their growth projections after taking into account the recent currency turmoil and high domestic interest rate environment.

The Malaysian ringgit has fallen more than 11 percent against the dollar over the past month due to heavy selling by offshore funds. The currency hit a 42-month low of 2.7930 against the dollar on Tuesday.
Heavy intervention by the central Bank Negara Malaysia in June to defend the ringgit, mopped up large funds from the banking system, pushing interbank rates sharply higher.
Malaysian exports in the first six months of this year rose by only 1.9 percent, to 98.4 billion ringgit against the same period of 1996.
